places.openingNote: Free for everyone. The farm warns there is deep water on site, so keep little ones close.
places.accessibilityNote: A hard-standing path means most of the farm is accessible for wheelchairs and buggies. Picnics welcome.

sessions.name: Farm Tots
sessions.notes: For under 5s and their parents or carers. Help look after the animals, then play and snack time. Check the farm's Facebook page for updates.

places.name: St Werburghs City Farm
places.openingNote: Open 7 days a week: 9am to 5pm in summer, 9am to 4pm in winter. Closed Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, Boxing Day, New Year's Eve and New Year's Day. Free entry; a £5 donation is encouraged but everyone is welcome.

featureNotes.playArea: Adventure play space and playground opposite the farm entrance, next to the café.

facilities.cafeNote: City Farm Cafe: Friday, Saturday, Sunday and Monday, 9.30am to 3.30pm. No reservations.

parking.note: Limited parking on Watercress Road; the farm suggests parking before the Mina Road tunnel and walking 2 minutes. No disabled bays, but you can call ahead to ask for a space near the entrance.

places.accessibilityNote: Entrance path has a steep ramp that some wheelchair users may need help with; a wooden ramp leads to the lower paddocks. Two accessible public toilets near the entrance (doors open outwards, may be small for larger powered wheelchairs).

places.name: Windmill Hill City Farm
places.openingNote: Farm and gardens open on bank holidays too, except for a short Christmas closure. Free entry; donations welcome. Paths can be muddy after rain.

featureNotes.animalFeeding: Please don't feed the animals. You can stroke animals that come to the fences, then wash hands with soap and water.
featureNotes.playArea: Play area with sand pit, climbing wall, climbing net and dragon swing, plus a digger park and fairy garden.

facilities.cafeNote: Open every day, 9am to 4.30pm. Kids menu. Buggy park outside (no buggies inside the café).

parking.note: No parking on site except one blue badge bay and a 20-minute drop-off point. Metered street parking on Philip Street, or the parking scheme at Asda.

places.accessibilityNote: The café, paths around the gardens, paddocks and animal pens are wheelchair accessible. Three accessible toilets. Blue badge holders can park free on Philip Street.

places.name: Blaise Museum
places.address: Blaise Castle Estate, Henbury Road, Bristol
places.openingNote: Open Thursday to Sunday, 11am to 4pm, from April to December (2 April to 31 December in 2026). Free entry; donations welcome. Has a dressing-up room for families. Set in Blaise Castle Estate parkland.

facilities.cafeNote: No café in the museum: the Blaise Estate café is near the car park entrance. The museum shop sells cold drinks, ice cream and snacks.

parking.note: Public car park on Henbury Road, about 300 yards from the museum. Bristol City Council parking charges apply.

places.accessibilityNote: Stairs to all floors and no lift. Wheelchair access to the ground floor with a portable ramp (ask staff). No wheelchair-accessible toilet. Toilets and baby change on the ground floor unless the Picture Room is booked for a private event.

places.name: Bristol Museum & Art Gallery
places.openingNote: Open Tuesday to Sunday, 10am to 5pm; closed Mondays. Free entry, no need to book; donations welcome. Some exhibitions need tickets. Gallery refurbishment may cause some noise and smells.

featureNotes.toddlerArea: Curiosity under-fives area (ground floor): a stage, puppets, games and stories. Also a dinosaur activity area on the first floor.

facilities.cafeNote: Ground-floor café, Tuesday to Sunday 10am to 4.30pm. Free picnic room at weekends and in school holidays.

parking.note: No museum car park. Nearest city car parks are West End (BS8 1EH) and Trenchard Street (BS1 5AN), about a 5-minute walk.

places.accessibilityNote: Level entry through electronic doors to the left of the main entrance, then a platform lift; lift to all public areas except Sea Dragons. Buggy park and extra-wide lockers for folded buggies. Breastfeeding welcome.

places.name: M Shed
places.openingNote: Open Tuesday to Sunday, 10am to 5pm; closed Mondays (it opened on some Mondays in the summer holidays). Free entry, no need to book; donations welcome. Steam train, boat and crane rides run on some dates (see what's on).

featureNotes.toddlerArea: Little M Shed: building bricks, books to share and a wooden train track table for pre-schoolers.

facilities.cafeNote: M Café, ground floor: Tuesday to Sunday 10am to 4.30pm, food 11am to 3pm. Kids bites and highchairs.

parking.note: No museum car park. Nearby car parks at The Grove (BS1 4RB) and Wapping Wharf (BS1 4RH), both with accessible spaces. Drop-off on Museum Street behind the museum.

places.accessibilityNote: Level entrances, level access to all galleries, three lifts, accessible toilets on every floor, buggy park. Free 'Little Bag of Calm' to borrow and an autism-friendly visual guide.
